title: Extension by zero of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $j\colon U\to X$ an open immersion.
The *extension by zero of module objects* is

$$
j_!:=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda_U}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X},
$$

restriction of scalars along $\alpha_j\colon j^*\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]) followed by the
linear extension by zero of [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek]. The underlying
sheaf of $j_!M$ is the extension by zero $j^{\Ab}_!M$ of the underlying sheaf of $M$,
and $j_!$ is additive and exact.

proof.text: Put $A=j^*\Lambda_X$ and $B=\Lambda_U$. By [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], $\alpha_j:A\to B$ is an isomorphism of ring objects. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], $R=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}$ sends a $B$-action $\gamma$ to $\gamma(\alpha_j\otimes M)$ and leaves underlying objects and morphisms unchanged. Restriction along $\alpha_j^{-1}$ is inverse to $R$: on a $B$-module with action $\gamma$ the composite action is $\gamma((\alpha_j\circ\alpha_j^{-1})\otimes M)=\gamma$, while on an $A$-module with action $\delta$ it is $\delta((\alpha_j^{-1}\circ\alpha_j)\otimes M)=\delta$. Both composites fix every morphism, and $R$ preserves zero morphisms because it leaves their underlying maps unchanged. In particular $R$ preserves kernels and cokernels: apply its inverse to a cone or cocone satisfying the zero-composite condition, use the original universal factorization, and apply $R$ back; these mutually inverse operations preserve the factorization equation and its uniqueness. Thus $R$ is exact.

source.place: Definition of the composite; proof, first sentence (restriction of scalars is exact), using the coefficient isomorphism of sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms

proof.text: Let $L=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!$ of [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek], whose domain is $\Mod_A$ and codomain is $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$. Consequently $j_!=L\circ R$ is a well-typed functor $\Mod_{\Lambda_U}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$. For the forgetful functors $V_U,V_X$, restriction leaves underlying sheaves and maps unchanged ([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]) and $L$ has underlying sheaf functor $j^{\Ab}_!$ ([def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek]). Hence $V_X(j_!M)=j^{\Ab}_!(V_UM)$, naturally in $M$, with the corresponding equality on morphisms.

source.place: Displayed definition and underlying-sheaf clause; proof, first two sentences

proof.text: By [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek], $L$ is exact. Given any short exact sequence of $\Lambda_U$-module objects, step 1 gives a short exact sequence after $R$, and applying $L$ gives a short exact sequence after $L\circ R=j_!$. This proves exactness of the composite without a further lemma about composition.

For module objects as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], the sum of two linear maps is linear: $(h+k)\gamma_M=h\gamma_M+k\gamma_M=\gamma_N(A\otimes h)+\gamma_N(A\otimes k)=\gamma_N(A\otimes(h+k))$. Zero and finite direct sums carry the zero and componentwise actions, with the usual inclusions and projections linear; hence they are zero objects and biproducts. Restriction is additive because it is the identity on underlying morphisms ([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]). The functor $L$ is a left adjoint by [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek]. The adjunction identifies maps out of $L(M\oplus N)$ with pairs of maps out of $LM,LN$, and maps out of $L0$ with a singleton, so $L$ preserves binary coproducts and the zero object. Every zero morphism factors through the zero object, so $L$ also preserves zero morphisms. Under the coproduct comparison isomorphism it preserves the biproduct projections: they are the maps $[1,0]$ and $[0,1]$ determined by the injections. Therefore it preserves the diagonal and codiagonal as well, and the identity $h+k=\nabla\circ(h\oplus k)\circ\Delta$ proves $L(h+k)=Lh+Lk$. It follows explicitly that $j_!(h+k)=L(Rh+Rk)=j_!h+j_!k$, and likewise $j_!(0)=0$. Thus $j_!$ is additive.
